headline: Your skin contains millions of sensors for pressure, temperature, pain, and texture
universal_truth: We understand through contact; connection requires touch
fun_facts: Skin is your largest organ—about 20 square feet in adults, weighing about 8 pounds
Fingertips have the highest density of touch receptors—about 2,500 per square centimeter
Touch is the first sense to develop in the womb and the last to fade as we age
discussion_questions: How important is physical touch to your wellbeing?
Why do you think touch is the first and last sense we have?
What textures do you find most comforting?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Right now, your skin is sensing: the pressure of your clothes, the temperature of the air, the texture of anything you're touching. Millions of sensors, constantly reporting. Skin is your largest organ—and your most constant source of information about the world.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: You can feel the difference between silk and sandpaper, a warm cup and cold glass. You sense pain before damage. How does skin distinguish so many different sensations with such precision?
cliff.prompt: How does skin sense different sensations?

options.text: Different types of nerve receptors specialize in pressure, temperature, pain, and vibration
options.response: Yes. Your skin contains multiple specialized receptor types, each tuned to specific sensations.

options.text: The brain interprets different intensities of a single touch signal
options.response: The brain interprets signals, but the sensors themselves are specialized...

q1.title: The Largest Organ
q1.script: Your skin covers about 20 square feet and weighs around 8 pounds. It's not just a wrapper—it's an active organ that senses, regulates temperature, produces vitamin D, and defends against pathogens. Skin is doing more than you know.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Largest Organ"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Fingertip Precision
q2.script: Your fingertips have about 2,500 touch receptors per square centimeter—the highest density anywhere on your body. That's why you can read Braille, thread a needle, or detect vibrations too subtle for other body parts. Fingertips are exquisitely sensitive.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: First and Last
q3.script: Touch is the first sense to develop in the womb—by 8 weeks, embryos respond to touch. It's also the last to fade as we age. From first to last, touch remains our most primal connection to the physical world.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Connection requires contact. Touch reminds us that we're physical beings in a physical world—and that our understanding grows through direct encounter. Don't just observe life; touch it.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 83. Tomorrow, we'll explore how your eyes see. Until then, pay attention to what your skin is telling you right now.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Touch Awareness - Feel What You're Feeling
growTrack.activity: For the next minute, close your eyes and notice everything your skin is sensing—pressure, temperature, textures, air movement. We often ignore this constant stream of information. What is your skin telling you right now?
